name: Repo Doctor
description:
repo-doctor diagnoses README "shape problems" — the hero never lands, install-to-first-success buries the lede, the "what is this" sentence assumes prior context, the badge row is louder than the content — and produces a prioritized punch list a maintainer can act on in an afternoon. Read-only by default; opens a PR only when the user explicitly asks.

Key features:
- 9-criterion rubric scored 1–5 with cited line numbers and one-line fixes
- Rubric weighting adapts to inferred repo category: library, CLI, framework, app, spec, or personal project
- Audience inference (working developers, newcomers, maintainers, mixed) — catches the most common shape problem: README pitched at the wrong audience for its category
- Punch list grouped P0 (blocking) / P1 (high-leverage) / P2 (nice-to-have)
- Three operating modes (Auto / Semi-auto / Manual) with the same conversational density tradeoff as repo-visuals
- Optional upstream PR with the punch list as the description; never auto-applies edits
longDescription:
Ships **1 skill**, `readme-doctor` (Audit a GitHub repo's README against best-practice patterns and produce a prioritized punch list of fixes).

Installs with `claude plugin install repo-doctor@claude-community` from `livlign/claude-skills` (`plugins/repo-doctor`).

A Claude Code plugin for diagnosing GitHub README problems — a structured audit against patterns that correlate with maintainer outcomes (hero presence, install-to-first-success length, "what is this in one sentence" clarity, audience-jargon match, drift signals), output as a prioritized punch list.
